% The URL of another document's PDF with xr and no hyperref, which takes it
% as xr-hyper does: with a prefix, with none, and through
% \externalcitedocument. The page builds, and each reference prints as
% without a URL: a label of an .aux that LaTeX wrote with its number or
% page, one of an .aux that tex4ht wrote, with its .xref, as a link to
% that document's page, and one of a file that does not exist yet as ??.
% A URL may hold an escaped \#.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{xr}
\externaldocument[X-]{test-xr/latex}[https://example.org/ext.pdf]
\externaldocument[T-]{test-xrurl/xr}[https://example.org/~a/b_c\#page=2]
\externaldocument{test-xr/plain}[https://example.org/plain.pdf]
\externalcitedocument[C-]{test-xr/plain}[https://example.org/cite.pdf]
\externaldocument[M-]{test-xrurl/none}[https://example.org/none.pdf]
\begin{document}
CaseG \ref{X-ss}, page \pageref{X-front}.

CaseH \ref{T-oss}.

CaseJ \ref{ss}, page \pageref{front}, cited \ref{C-s}.

CaseN \ref{M-a}.

\section{Here}\label{here}
Local \ref{here}.
\end{document}
